Analects.label: Middle Warring States (c. 400-300 BCE)
Analects.note: Consensus: large portions composed during the Warring States period; final form mid-Han. Layered composition (Brooks & Brooks accretion 479-249 BCE); assigned to mid-WS by dominant composition stratum.

Gongsun_Longzi.label: Late Warring States (c. 300-221 BCE)
Gongsun_Longzi.note: Essays associated with Gongsun Long (c. 320-250 BCE); 6 of 14 original essays extant, some possibly later.

Guanzi.label: Qin-Western Han (221 BCE-9 CE)
Guanzi.note: Compiled early Han (received text edited by Liu Xiang c. 26 BCE); 'proto-Guanzi' c. 250 BCE; Sato dates most chapters late WS vs Rickett's Han dates for some. Assigned by final compilation.

Guiguzi.label: Late Warring States (c. 300-221 BCE)
Guiguzi.note: Compiled between late WS and end of Han; books I-II reflect genuine WS rhetoric corpus attributed to a 4th-c. teacher; book III a later addition. Least-bad: late WS.

Han_Feizi.label: Late Warring States (c. 300-221 BCE)
Han_Feizi.note: Most of 55 chapters mid-3rd c. BCE; Laozi-commentary chapters 20-21 generally considered later addenda.

Huainanzi.label: Qin-Western Han (221 BCE-9 CE)
Huainanzi.note: Compiled from essays of the court of Liu An, Prince of Huainan, presented to Emperor Wu before 139 BCE; final chapter possibly posthumous.

Kongzi_Jiayu.label: Qin-Western Han (221 BCE-9 CE)
Kongzi_Jiayu.note: Book existed since at least early Han, listed in Yiwenzhi; received version a Wang Su (195-256 CE) recension; Dingzhou/Shuanggudui finds show Han-era material underlying it. Dated as Han compilation.

Laozi.label: Middle Warring States (c. 400-300 BCE)
Laozi.note: Guodian slips c. 300 BCE attest a 4th-c. version; conservative modern estimates put received text mid-3rd c. BCE consolidating older sayings; traditional ascription to a 6th-c. Lao Dan rejected by most. Least-bad: 4th c. BCE.

Liezi.label: Post-Han compilation (3rd-4th c. CE recension, with older layers)
Liezi.note: Many Chinese and Western scholars hold the current text's content was compiled c. 4th c. CE (Zhang Zhan recension); Han-era attestation of a Liezi book and possible WS underlying layers keep dating contested.

Liji.label: Qin-Western Han (221 BCE-9 CE)
Liji.note: Diverse compilation: some chapters pre-Han (Guodian 'Black Robes' c. 300 BCE; parallels in Xunzi, Lushi Chunqiu), others Former Han; received compilation edited by Dai Sheng (Western Han).

Liutao.label: Late Warring States (c. 300-221 BCE)
Liutao.note: Modern historians nominally date final composition to the WS period; some argue vestiges of ancient Qi thought, others a later (Han) compilation; least-bad: late WS.

Lushi_Chunqiu.label: Late Warring States (c. 300-221 BCE)
Lushi_Chunqiu.note: Compiled c. 239 BCE under Lu Buwei; almanac postface dated 239 BCE; other parts completed c. 235 BCE.

Mencius.label: Middle Warring States (c. 400-300 BCE)
Mencius.note: Believed written late 4th c. BCE, largely by disciples of Mencius (c. 371-289).

Mozi.label: Middle Warring States (c. 400-300 BCE)
Mozi.note: Core chapters derive from Mozi (5th c. figure) and early Mohists; 'Dialectical Chapters' patently 3rd c. BCE; 7 chapters of much later date. Assigned by core triads (4th c.).

Shangjunshu.label: Late Warring States (c. 300-221 BCE)
Shangjunshu.note: 3rd-c. BCE text overall (Pines: some chapters from Shang Yang's lifetime or shortly after, composition took over a century, ch. 15 late); earliest Legalist corpus after the attributed layers.

Sima_Fa.label: Middle Warring States (c. 400-300 BCE)
Sima_Fa.note: Developed in Qi during the 4th century BCE (mid-WS), though traditional attribution to Sima Rangju (6th c.) is doubted.

Sunzi_Bingfa.label: Early: Spring and Autumn to early Warring States (pre-c. 400 BCE)
Sunzi_Bingfa.note: Traditionally late Spring and Autumn (c. 5th c. BCE); earliest parts at least a century after the legendary 6th-c. Sun Wu. Significant minority dates it later (WS); least-bad reading: pre-400 BCE core.

Wei_Liaozi.label: Late Warring States (c. 300-221 BCE)
Wei_Liaozi.note: Present form around end of 4th c. BCE; Yinqueshan Han-tomb find confirms pre-Han transmission; authorship (student of Lord Shang vs Qin advisor) unresolved.

Wuzi.label: Middle Warring States (c. 400-300 BCE)
Wuzi.note: No consensus on final composition date; core nominally composed around Wu Qi's lifetime (440-381 BCE), mid-WS.

Xiaojing.label: Late Warring States (c. 300-221 BCE)
Xiaojing.note: Most likely late WS to early Han (4th-3rd c. BCE); assigned to late WS as least-bad reading of the straddling date.

Xunzi.label: Late Warring States (c. 300-221 BCE)
Xunzi.note: Writings of Xun Kuang (3rd c. BCE) and disciples; redacted into 32 bundles by Liu Xiang (1st c. CE).

Zhongyong.label: Qin-Western Han (221 BCE-9 CE)
Zhongyong.note: Traditionally Zisi (5th c. BCE), doubted since Cui Shu; modern scholars hold parts were written/edited at the Qin-Han transition.

Zhuangzi.label: Middle Warring States (c. 400-300 BCE)
Zhuangzi.note: Inner chapters associated with Zhuang Zhou (c. 369-286 BCE); outer/miscellaneous chapters later (school of Zhuangzi, some pre-Han to Han); final compilation Han. Assigned by inner-chapter stratum.

source_claim: No single ancient proponent: this is the modern 'era' comparator pre-registered in the lab's hypothesis H-C1 (six-schools taxonomy vs era/region/genre), built from modern transmitted-text dating scholarship (the Loewe 'Early Chinese Texts' tradition; Brooks & Brooks accretional model; Guodian-informed Laozi dating; Pines on the Book of Lord Shang; Sato on the Guanzi; Graham-school view of the Liezi). Class set: 5 composition strata from Spring-and-Autumn/early Warring States to post-Han compilation. Each book is assigned by its period of composition/final compilation per the cited literature; where dating is disputed the majority/least-bad reading is taken and confidence is marked 'contested'.
title: Era / stratigraphic partition of early Chinese masters literature (composition/final-compilation dating)
